liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **SMag** (2 reviews): Sugar Magnolia is insane, with Bobby and Jerry dueling on guitar near the end of the main jam; Sugar Magnolia was an excellent closer [17][19]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Scarlet into Fire was so energetic the reviewer expected lightning to strike the building; Scarlet-Fire, Terrapin and Sugar Magnolia singled out as highlights [16][23]
- **BT Wind** (1 review): Return to the song's original lyrics was received well by the crowd [14]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Truckin' into Terrapin Station described as blazing [16]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Described as gorgeous; Truckin' into Terrapin also called a nice twist [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **ROR**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]
- **BT Wind**: back after 1288 archived shows (6700 days); mythic rare: 2 archived performances [26]
- **Fire**: rare: 13 archived performances [26]
- **TOO**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]
- **SMag**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]

## The recordings

- **gd1990-09-14.schoeps.brotman.9623.shnf** (recommended): source not stated; 20 songs; 177 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1990-09-14.mtx.hansokolow.97443.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 18 songs; 178 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: A few spots of digital noise in the second set were patched from a cassette master [2]
- **gd1990-09-14.nak300.andrewf.92017.flac16**: audience recording; 19 songs; 172 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [6]. Said about its sound: Brief distortion in Stranger at 2:44 was softened with Soundforge [6]
- **gd1990-09-14.141164.OTS.AKG.Ackerman.Miller.Noel.t-flac1648**: audience recording; 18 songs; 176 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [7]. Said about its sound: Slight frequency oddness between songs in the first set, nothing serious [7]
- **gd90-09-14.schoeps-fob.wiley.11810.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 176 min; rated 3.88/5 by 8 [8]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is very clear, among the better audience tapes; This audience copy is described as about as close to soundboard quality as any audience tape gets; Audience recording sounds broader than the flat soundboard, with the Garden's echo; the crowd eruption after the New York City line is audible [23][24][25]
- **gd90-09-14.sbd.fishman.7769.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 168 min; rated 4.14/5 by 13 [12]. Said about its sound: Soundboard recording is near perfect; first cut has fumbling at the start, so beginning at Sugaree sounds better [18]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended; says it was Vince's first Madison Square Garden show with the band, and his keyboard tone was poor [14]
- By this night Welnick sounded as if he'd toured with the band for ages, though his sound was awkward at first [15]
- The keyboardist played like a virtuoso, and his small keyboard tone oddly complemented the band [18]
- Reviewer recalls exposed ceilings in Garden hallways and a crowded, awkward exit route that night [19]
- Commenter believes Bill Graham gave the intro, with Healy adding vocal effects; speculative, since the commenter wasn't present [22]
- First Garden show since Brent died; the original members seemed determined to prove they still had plenty left [23]
- John Scher introduces the band, and they launch energetically from the start [25]
- Opening night of a six-night run at an arena described as very easy to sneak into [7]
- Reviewer calls the 1990 Garden run among the best single-venue runs ever, with the band improving noticeably each night [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1990-09-14.schoeps.brotman.9623.shnf**: taped by Dave Brotman FOB DFC, (Section 2, row 15, seat 1); source: Schoeps MK4/CMC3 (ortf/110deg)>Oade PS>Oade Mod. SV255 (MIT reference XLR interconnects). [1]. Also: Tapers befriended the head security guard and made him a D5 copy every night [1]
- **gd1990-09-14.mtx.hansokolow.97443.flac16**: transferred by hansokolow; source: matrix of DSBD: shnid=74405 and DAUD: shnid=88942 by hansokolow using ProTools [2]. Also: Matrix made by hansokolow in ProTools from DAT sources, transferred and mastered by Charlie Miller; Ambient recording by Sean Weber and Rick Katseff using B&K 4011s in ORTF, Grace preamp, to Panasonic SV250 [2]
- **gd1990-09-14.nak300.andrewf.92017.flac16**: taped by Andrew F.; transferred by Andrew F.; source: OTS AUD: Nakamichi CM300's w/CP4 shotguns > patched thru one Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX90/100, with no Dolby. [6]. Also: Tape-flip gaps after Terrapin's Jam and in Sugar Magnolia were patched from the ShnID-11810 source [6]
- **gd1990-09-14.141164.OTS.AKG.Ackerman.Miller.Noel.t-flac1648**: taped by Ron Ackerman; transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Noel; source: flac16/48kHz ; Master Audience Recording & Transfer by Ray Ackerman: AKG 460B/CK63 ULS -> AKG B18 phantom power unit -> Panasonic SV250 -> DAT (OTS); Transfer… [7]
- **gd90-09-14.schoeps-fob.wiley.11810.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD(Schoeps)> DAT> CDR>WAV>SHN [8]
- **gd90-09-14.sbd.fishman.7769.sbeok.shnf**: source: Analog SBD>DAT>CDR>WAV>SHN [12]
